title: Tennis Star Coco Gauff Says Rival Has More Pressure Than Her
summary:
Have you ever felt like everyone expects you to win? Tennis star Coco Gauff says her friend and rival Alexandra Eala has even more pressure than she does. Eala is from the Philippines, and she's the first Filipino player to win a big tennis title. Last month, she won a WTA singles title, and now she's ranked 18th in the world. That's a huge deal!

At the US Open, Eala lost in the third round, and she got emotional talking about all the support she gets from her home country. Gauff, who is ranked number four, said she can't really understand what Eala goes through. "She has more pressure than I do," Gauff said.

Why? Because Eala is breaking barriers. She's doing for the Philippines what boxing legend Manny Pacquiao did. Gauff said she's lucky to be from the US, where there are lots of tennis stars to look up to. "I can't really empathise," she said.

Eala has made history before. Last year, she became the first Filipino to win a match at the US Open. This year, she reached the fourth round at Wimbledon. After that, she went home to a big party thrown by the president of the Philippines! Filipino fans are everywhere now, waving flags at her matches.

Gauff respects Eala a lot. She said, "From the outside looking in, she has more pressure." But Eala seems to handle it well. Next time you feel pressure, remember that even famous athletes feel it too!
why_it_matters: Pressure is something every kid can understand — at school, in sports, or at home — and Eala shows that even when people expect a lot from you, you can keep going and make others proud.

background_read: Tennis is a worldwide sport, but some countries have many more tennis champions than others.
Alexandra Eala comes from the Philippines (a country made of many islands in Southeast Asia), where she is the first player to reach such high levels in women's tennis.
Boxer Manny Pacquiao (a Filipino sports hero) was famous for putting the Philippines in the spotlight, and Eala is now doing something similar for tennis.
Article_Structure: WHO: Coco Gauff, ranked No. 4, and Alexandra Eala, ranked No. 18 and described as her friend and rival.
WHAT: Gauff says Eala has more pressure because Eala is breaking barriers for Philippine tennis.
WHERE: At international tennis events, including the US Open, where Eala lost in the third round.
WHY: Eala fills big hopes for her whole home country, and Gauff says the US has many stars while the Philippines has few.

perspectives.description: She respects Eala and says the pressure on Eala is bigger than on her because Eala represents a whole country with few tennis legends.
She feels emotional about the support from the Philippines, but she seems to handle the pressure well.
Seeing a home player win big titles feels historic, like watching Manny Pacquiao in boxing, and it fills young fans with pride.
